title: Working With DOM Properties
learning_outcomes: Explain the role of working with dom properties in a jQuery application.
Apply the .prop() method in a small example and describe its expected result.
Verify boolean properties with an explicit test or browser observation.
status_note: Draft generated from the attached syllabus and official references; requires lesson-by-lesson technical review, local execution, accessibility checks, and editorial approval.

content.intro: In this lesson, you will work through working with dom properties with a focused jQuery example. The subtopics below preserve the supplied curriculum coverage and connect the API idea to a small browser interface.
content.why_it_matters: This topic is useful because it turns the .prop() method into a repeatable implementation choice. Attributes describe markup; properties represent current DOM state. For example, checked and selected are runtime properties, while data-* attributes are markup strings and jQuery data values are a separate cache.

common_mistakes: Assuming a selector matched an element without checking the collection length.
Confusing jQuery collections with native DOM elements or live properties with markup attributes.
Using .html() with untrusted data or assuming client-side validation enforces server rules.
Treating a demo snippet as production-ready without testing failure and accessibility states.
